articles.title: “Arising Out Of” Is Causal Link, Without This, Liability Falls; Alleged Murder Not Compensable Under MV Act Without Proof Connecting Vehicle to Death: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that compensation for death under the Motor Vehicles (MV) Act requires proof of a causal link between the vehicle and the incident. Without establishing this connection, liability does not arise. The Court clarified that while compensation proceedings follow a broad interpretation, some evidence linking the vehicle to the death is essential. This decision impacts how future claims under the MV Act are adjudicated.
articles.raw_summary: The Court held that although the expression  arising out of  receives a broad interpretation and compensation proceedings are governed by the standard of preponderance of probabilities, the existence of some link whatsoever between the car, and the death had to be established. articles.summary: The U.S. has seen a significant rise in measles cases in 2026 compared to 2025, with experts attributing the surge to declining vaccination rates and public amnesia about the disease's severity. Health officials warn that measles can be life-threatening, highlighting the importance of immunization. The situation may prompt discussions on vaccination policies or public health measures in countries like India, which faces similar challenges.

articles.title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
articles.summary: Lenacapavir is a new HIV prevention drug that requires only two injections per year, offering a significant improvement over daily pills for high-risk groups. Its effectiveness depends on ensuring sufficient supply and reaching the intended at-risk populations. The drug's long-term impact on reducing HIV infections in India will depend on public health policies and implementation strategies.
articles.raw_summary: Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

articles.summary: US President Donald Trump announced plans to launch a tariff investigation against the European Union in response to EU fines imposed on US tech companies, including Google. The move follows a recent ruling where Google lost a case in the EU. The dispute highlights growing global tensions over digital market regulations and tech company accountability.

articles.title: Oil prices jump as Hormuz, Red Sea crises deepen
articles.summary: Renewed attacks on shipping routes in the Gulf of Hormuz and the Red Sea have disrupted global oil supplies, pushing crude oil prices back above $100 per barrel. For India, which relies heavily on oil imports, this could impact fuel costs, inflation, and trade balances, potentially prompting policy discussions on energy security or strategic reserves.
articles.raw_summary: Renewed strikes on shipping in the Gulf and the Red Sea have dealt a fresh double blow to global oil markets, with the price of crude oil once again passing $100 a barrel. DW examines what could push prices even higher.

The issue underscores broader debates about balancing technological growth with sustainability and energy management.
articles.raw_summary: Rapid data center construction across the US, fueled by AI, comes with serious threats to the environment, public health and energy supply. Local opposition has blocked or delayed dozens of projects.

It suggests that these exams, which are critical for academic and career opportunities, have become unreliable due to systemic failures. The piece frames this as a generational issue affecting Gen-Z students and calls for systemic reforms in the education sector.
articles.raw_summary: A network of corruption in the education system washed away your efforts & the entrance exams that were meant to test your mettle turned out to be a mirage

articles.title: Opinion: Opinion | Why Dharmendra Pradhan's Exit Is Also About An 'Age' Problem
articles.summary: India's Gen Z can vote at 18, graduate soon afterwards, and even hold bureaucratic positions after 21. What they still can't do is contest elections before they turn 25.

articles.title: ETtech Explainer: Why PhonePe’s UPI lead lags Paytm’s profits
articles.summary: PhonePe, a leading UPI payments platform in India, saw its revenue grow but its net loss widen in FY26, while Paytm achieved profitability despite revenue growth. Paytm's success is attributed to better cost management and financial services distribution, whereas PhonePe's UPI leadership has not translated into strong monetization. The article highlights the need for PhonePe to improve operational efficiency and diversify products to sustain growth in India's competitive digital payments market.
articles.raw_summary: PhonePe's revenue grew while its net loss widened significantly in FY26. Paytm's revenue increased and it achieved profitability against a prior year loss. Paytm's cost management and financial services distribution drove its faster monetization. PhonePe's UPI dominance offers distribution but faces monetization challenges. Future growth for PhonePe hinges on operational efficiency and product diversification.

articles.title: What is the AI Kill Switch Act? Why US lawmakers want the power to shut down rogue AI models
articles.summary: US lawmakers are proposing the AI Kill Switch Act, a bill that would give the government the power to shut down dangerous AI models. The legislation aims to create an emergency control framework for powerful AI systems, requiring companies to maintain intervention capabilities. This raises questions about government authority over AI and national control over advanced technology. The move could influence global AI governance, including India's approach to regulating AI.
articles.raw_summary: The proposed US legislation seeks to create an emergency control framework for some of the world's most powerful artificial intelligence systems. It could require major AI companies to maintain the ability to intervene when models become dangerous, while raising wider questions about government authority, technological dependence and national control over advanced AI.

articles.title: Can India go from making generic drugs to discovering the next blockbuster medicine?
articles.summary: India has built a global reputation for making affordable generic medicines, but the next phase of its pharmaceutical industry could be about discovering new drugs. A BCG-HealthKois report says rising research funding, patent filings and biotech startups are laying the groundwork, though the country still has a long way to go before it can compete with the world's biggest pharmaceutical innovators.

articles.title: What is the Tenth Schedule? The anti-defection law at the centre of Kapil Sibal's Supreme Court plea
articles.summary: Senior advocate Kapil Sibal has filed a plea in the Supreme Court challenging the interpretation of the Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, which governs anti-defection laws. Sibal argues that legislators should not be able to avoid disqualification by exploiting the merger provision. The case could impact how anti-defection rules are enforced in Parliament and state legislatures.
